content:
ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • sev=2 • Customer-reported possible cross-tenant prompt exposure on Dedicated pool dp-834. PagerDuty: https://pd.example/XYZ :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Triggered on-call: Maya O'Neill (primary). Policy: "Customer isolation + forensics".

Maya O'Neill: on it. acknowledging. Samir, can you confirm which tenant and what evidence the customer sent?

Arman Kapoor: I have the customer's support ticket (cust-834). They pasted a convo that contains a long prompt that references another customer's internal product names. They attached a screenshot and a few request IDs: rID: c834-2026-03-15-09-12, rID: c912-2026-03-15-09-09

Samir Patel: thanks. i'm pulling routing logs for dp-834. giving ETA ~5m.

Dave Huang: if this is cross-tenant routing, likely misrouted to a shared host / routing rule. first quick mitigation: remove dp-834 from the shared ingress pool and pin cust-834 to a fresh dedicated pool.

Liz Chen: tagging security. need to preserve forensic logs (no restart that wipes cache). please do NOT rotate keys or restart services unless we snapshot logs.

Maya O'Neill: checklist - (1) preserve logs, (2) triage scope (how many requests), (3) immediate mitigation (isolate customer), (4) customer comms.

Samir Patel: logs pulled: looks like two requests with matching KV cache keys that overlap between tenant IDs — timestamps align. I see a routing decision: route->pool-shared-03 -> host-12.

Dave Huang: confirm: pool-shared-03 should not have dp-834 assigned. running quick audit command:

Dave Huang: ```bash
# list routing entries for pool-shared-03
redwoodctl routing list --pool pool-shared-03 --json | jq '.entries[] | {tenant, pool, host}'
```

Samir Patel: output shows stale entry for tenant cust-912 referencing dp-834 on host-12. looks like a stale mapping from yesterday's scale-down.

Maya O'Neill: okay we need a two-step mitigation: (A) remove stale mapping so no new misroutes, (B) create isolated pool and migrate cust-834 traffic.

Dave Huang: working on (A). removing mapping now.

Dave Huang: ```bash
redwoodctl routing remove --pool pool-shared-03 --tenant cust-912 --force
# verify
redwoodctl routing list --pool pool-shared-03 | grep cust-912 || echo "cleared"
```

infra-deploy-bot: routing.remove started by dave.huang at 2026-03-15T09:28:47Z. job_id=job-5591

Samir Patel: after removal, I rechecked logs: no new hits showing cross-tenant matches in the last 3 minutes.

Maya O'Neill: proceed with (B) isolated pool creation. Dave, can you spin up a dedicated dp-834-isolate with same capacity? Mark it as customer-only.

Dave Huang: spinning up. command: ```bash
redwoodctl pool create --name dp-834-isolate --hardware a100-40gb --tags customer:isolate,cust-834
``` ETA 4m.

Liz Chen: while that's provisioning, collect KV cache keys for affected time window to check potential exposure surface. Samir, can you dump keys for host-12 from 09:04-09:13?

Samir Patel: running dump now. ```bash
redis-cli -h host-12.lan --rdb /tmp/host12.rdb && s3 cp /tmp/host12.rdb s3://forensics/cust-834/host12-0904-0913.rdb
```

Samir Patel: dump complete, uploaded to s3://forensics/cust-834/host12-0904-0913.rdb. checksum sha256: abc123...

Arman Kapoor: flagged for legal/comms. I'll draft a short customer message: apologize, say we found routing anomaly, we've isolated environment and are investigating. want to confirm no sensitive data leaked to other customers.

Maya O'Neill: good. initial customer note (send in 30m): "We've isolated your traffic, are collecting forensic logs, and will update within 4 hours. Do not retry affected requests." Keep it short.

Liz Chen: forensics update: after scanning RDB, I see two keys with identical prefix used by cust-912 and cust-834 — likely shared prefix collision in our prefixing fallback with older runtime. Risk: small chance of partial prompt reuse. Need to check whether any downstream outputs were returned to the wrong tenant.

Dave Huang: check response logs for rID c834-2026-03-15-09-12 and c912-2026-03-15-09-09.

Samir Patel: response logs show both returned outputs at ~09:09. Comparing hashes... different output bodies, but one contains a variable that references cust-912 internal product name. That suggests input material from cust-912 was present when cust-834 request executed.

Maya O'Neill: severity: escalate to P1->P0? It's customer-sensitive (enterprise VPC). Arman, do we have contract/SLAs implications?

Arman Kapoor: enterprise SLA and data isolation clause. legal loop required. I'm escalating to account security and legal now.

Liz Chen: mitigation steps recommended:
- immediately purge shared KV cache entries for affected prefix across hosts
- enforce tenant-scoped cache keys (hotfix)
- isolate pool and move traffic (in progress)
- rotate any credentials if there's risk to secret material
- full forensic report and customer notification draft

Dave Huang: purging cache now: ```bash
# purge keys matching prefix for affected window
redwoodctl cache purge --host host-12 --prefix "tenant_prefix_*" --time-range "2026-03-15T09:00:00Z/2026-03-15T09:20:00Z" --confirm
```

infra-deploy-bot: cache.purge job job-5596 started by dave.huang

Samir Patel: purge completed on host-12, host-13, host-14. Verified no entries for that prefix remain.

Maya O'Neill: good. Dave, after dp-834-isolate is up, move cust-834 traffic and mark dp-834 as quarantined.

Dave Huang: dp-834-isolate is ready. migrating routing: ```bash
redwoodctl routing update --tenant cust-834 --pool dp-834-isolate --confirm
```

ops-bot: Migration event: cust-834 -> dp-834-isolate at 2026-03-15T09:42:31Z.

Samir Patel: monitoring traffic now. all new requests for cust-834 hitting dp-834-isolate. no cross-tenant hits observed.

Liz Chen: security note: we need a temporary customer-safe remediation plan: 1) full key rotation if any secrets were included 2) optional offer to re-run requests in isolated environment 3) 72-hour forensic report delivery.

Arman Kapoor: sending customer a short update now: "We identified an internal routing/cache anomaly affecting a small number of requests. We've isolated your environment, purged caches, and are performing a full forensic analysis. We'll update within 4 hours and follow up with a detailed report. If you want, we can replay requests in an isolated environment for you."

Maya O'Neill: handoff: I'm keeping ownership until forensics done. Samir/Dave continue logs & remediation. Liz lead on forensics. Arman lead on customer comms. I'll coordinate with legal.

Liz Chen: initial forensic summary (so far): 2 affected requests, 1 exposed token-like string (low-entropy), no confirmed secrets exfiltration. Full scan in progress.

Dave Huang: sched note: we'll patch runtime to enforce tenant-scoped cache keys this afternoon and backport to all regions. PR in progress.

Maya O'Neill: action items logged. next update in 1 hour or earlier if material changes.

Arman Kapoor: customer responded: appreciates quick action, wants timeline for full report. I told them 4 hours for initial findings, 72 hours for full report.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE • severity maintained at P1 • active participants: Maya, Samir, Dave, Liz, Arman.

Maya O'Neill: thanks everyone. keep posting logs and any anomalies in this thread.

Samir Patel: adding forensic artifacts to ticket: s3://forensics/cust-834/ (rdb, logs, routing-dump). I'll attach checksums and commands used.

Liz Chen: legal requested we retain raw artifacts; legal.contact: legal@redwood.example.

Maya O'Neill: closing interim mitigation window. We'll keep thread open until final report. :white_check_mark:
